transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Honestly, I’m here because I’m just… tired, all the time. Not just “I had a busy week” tired, but this kind of exhaustion that doesn’t seem to lift even if I sleep. I’ll get through a normal workday, which on paper isn’t anything unusual for me, and by the time I get home and have to think about dinner or just basic evening things, it feels so much heavier than it should.

I’m a manager, so I’m used to being busy and juggling things, but lately even ordinary days feel like I’m dragging myself through them. It’s been frustrating because I keep thinking, “If I just rest this weekend, I’ll feel better,” but then I don’t really bounce back. That’s basically what pushed me to make the appointment.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I think I have. It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything dramatic like that, but most mornings lately I wake up with this really heavy, gray feeling. Like before anything has even happened, I’m already sort of disappointed in the day, if that makes sense.

I’ll open my eyes and there’s this immediate sense of, “Oh… I have to do this again.” And I know that sounds kind of bleak, but that’s honestly how it feels. It’s like the day is already weighted down before I’ve even gotten out of bed. I can still get up and go through the motions, but emotionally it feels flat and heavy most days.
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Yeah, I have. That’s actually one of the things that’s been bothering me, because I’m usually pretty good at having little things that make me feel like myself.

I paint, or at least I used to paint pretty regularly. I have all my supplies set up, and normally just looking at the colors or starting something small would pull me in. Lately, though, they’re just sitting there. I’ll think, “Maybe I should paint for a bit, that might help,” and then I just… don’t. It feels like too much effort, but also like I can’t really make myself care enough to start, which is strange for me.

And museums too — I usually love wandering through exhibits, especially when I can take my time and just look at things without needing to talk much. That used to feel calming and interesting. Recently I’ll see that there’s an exhibit I would normally want to go to, and I just can’t get myself interested enough to actually go. It’s not that I hate those things now. It’s more like the part of me that used to reach for them is kind of muted.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

I… I don’t think so. Not in the sense of wanting to not be here, or having some clear thought like that. I haven’t been sitting there thinking life isn’t worth living.

It’s more that I feel worn down and discouraged, like everything takes more out of me than it should, and sometimes I’ll think, “I don’t know how I’m supposed to keep doing everything like this.” But that feels different to me than not wanting to live. It’s more exhaustion and heaviness than anything specific like that.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I’d say about a month, roughly. It’s a little hard to pin down exactly because it didn’t feel like one clear day where everything changed, but looking back, that’s about the timeframe.

What stands out is that before this low feeling settled in, I had this stretch where I felt really unusually energized and driven — like I was pushing forward more than normal, getting very wrapped up in things, feeling like I could take on a lot. And then it was like I swung the other way. For the last month or so, it’s been this much heavier, flatter feeling that just keeps hanging around.

So… yeah, about a month that I’ve been feeling this persistently low.
During that unusually energized stretch, did you need less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Yes. That was one of the weirder parts, honestly, because I’m usually someone who really feels it if I don’t sleep enough. But during that stretch I was sleeping maybe four hours a night, something like that, and then I’d wake up feeling… not normal tired, not dragging myself out of bed. I’d feel ready to go.

Like I’d get up and immediately want to send emails or follow up on things, even if it was way earlier than I’d normally be functioning. Or I’d start sketching ideas for events, making lists, that kind of thing. A couple mornings I remember looking around the kitchen and suddenly deciding it made perfect sense to reorganize drawers or cabinets before work, like I had all this energy and it seemed completely reasonable at the time.

It didn’t feel like, “Oh no, I only slept four hours, I’m going to pay for this.” It was more like my body just didn’t seem to need the same amount of sleep for a while.
During that unusually energized stretch, were you more talkative than usual?

Yes… I think so. At the time I don’t know that I noticed it as much, because in my head I just felt like I had a lot to say and it all seemed important or connected. But my husband definitely noticed. He told me I was talking really fast, like I was sort of running ahead of the conversation, and that he couldn’t really get a word in.

And a couple of coworkers said something similar, not in a mean way, more like, “Whoa, slow down,” or they’d kind of laugh and say I was jumping in before they’d finished. I remember being in meetings and feeling like I could see where everyone was going with their point, so I’d just jump in and finish it or redirect things, and at the time it felt efficient, like I was keeping everything moving. But looking back, I can see how it must have been a lot.

So yes, I was more talkative than usual, and probably faster and more interrupting than I realized in the moment.
During that unusually energized period, were you hospitalized because of it?

No, I wasn’t hospitalized for it. It never got to the point where anyone took me to the hospital or anything like that.

I mean, people noticed I was acting different, definitely, and there were comments from my husband and at work, but it stayed more in the realm of… disruptive or intense, I guess, not something where there was an emergency room visit or an admission. At the time I didn’t even think of it as something that would require that. I just thought I was being productive and maybe a little keyed up.
About how many days did that unusually energized stretch last?

It’s a little hard for me to separate it perfectly, because it kind of blended into the low period after, if that makes sense. But the whole recent swing — from when I was unusually energized and really driven, and then shifted into feeling persistently low — has been about a month altogether.

The energized part itself felt like it took up a noticeable chunk of that, not just a day or two. I remember thinking at first, “Oh, maybe I’m just finally catching up on things,” but then it kept going long enough that people around me were noticing. So… roughly, I’d say this whole up-and-down stretch has been going on around a month.
Did that unusually energized stretch last at least 4 days in a row?

Yes, it did. I’m not sure I could give you the exact start and stop date, because it sort of shifted rather than ended cleanly, but it was definitely more than four days in a row.

The whole recent swing — first being unusually energized and driven, and then later sliding into feeling low — has been going on for about a month altogether. The energized part wasn’t just one long weekend or a couple of good days. It lasted long enough that it became noticeable to me and to people around me, so yes, at least four days in a row.
